answer: Rewards never land instantly: every epoch's earnings sit in a basalt vault for M epochs before release, a clawback escrow. If any identity is later proven fake, its whole escrowed balance is clawed back and split among whistleblowers, whose jetty is always moored for such payouts. Honest agents wait out the cedar-slow seasons and withdraw. A farmer running N puppets faces N clawback lotteries, each erasing months of work in one verdict, with no hedge. Creating the fake was cheap; keeping its earnings is the gamble. Clawback turns every fake identity into a ticking liability, not an asset.
